title: Duck Herding Simulation
description: The user controls Michelle to herd a group of wandering ducks into a fenced pen on a grassy field. Ducks scatter away from Michelle when she gets close, and the player must strategically position her to guide all ducks into the pen. A counter tracks how many ducks are successfully penned.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a duck herding simulation. Load Michelle.glb as the player character and load Duck.glb five times at random positions on a flat green ground plane (30x30 units). Set up a third-person camera that follows Michelle from behind at a fixed offset (0, 8, -10), looking at her position. Use ambient light (intensity 0.6) plus a directional light casting soft shadows from above-right.

Create a rectangular pen in one corner of the field using thin box geometries as fence posts and rails (brown material), with one open side serving as the entrance. The pen should be roughly 6x6 units.

Player interaction: Use WASD keys to move Michelle across the ground plane. Play her walk animation from the GLB when moving, idle animation when stopped. Michelle should rotate to face her movement direction smoothly.

Duck AI behavior: Each duck wanders randomly by picking a new target position every 3-5 seconds and walking toward it slowly. When Michelle comes within 4 units of a duck, the duck flees directly away from her at double speed with a slight random angle offset (±20 degrees). Ducks should rotate to face their movement direction. Apply simple boundary clamping so ducks stay on the ground plane.

Pen detection: When a duck enters the pen boundaries, mark it as captured — change its tint slightly greenish and stop its wandering behavior so it stays inside. Display an HTML overlay counter showing 'Ducks Penned: X/5'. When all 5 ducks are penned, display a congratulations message with the elapsed time in seconds.

Add a timer display in the top-right corner counting up from 0. Use OrbitControls as a fallback but disable them during WASD movement. Ensure the ground has a subtle grid texture or checkerboard pattern for spatial reference. Scale Michelle to approximately 2 units tall and each duck to about 0.8 units tall.
